metadata.title: Bug fix regarding import/export not being executed

discussion_timeline.author: smistad
discussion_timeline.body:
Adding mIsModified=true has no effect, because it "shadows" the original variable from the ProcessObject class.
The correct use is setModified(true); in functions that modify the PO.

It is true that openslide reads data as BGR, however that should be handled in the getLevelAsImage function: https://github.com/smistad/FAST/blob/master/source/FAST/Data/Access/ImagePyramidAccess.cpp#L182

discussion_timeline.author: andreped
discussion_timeline.body: I agree. I have adjusted for your comments in the most recent commit.

discussion_timeline.author: andreped
discussion_timeline.body: I have made some futher modifications. I have marked the new changes in **bold** in the initial comment.

discussion_timeline.author: smistad
discussion_timeline.body:
[source/FAST/Algorithms/ImagePatch/PatchStitcher.cpp] I think this is too low, and may cause issues for your other WSI pipelines. Like patch-wise classification. If the resulting image of patch-wise classification is higher than 1024x1024, then that pipeline will fail for the same reason as it failed for "high"-res segmentation with 8192x8192 resolution. 
Also, creating an image pyramid for a 1024x1024 image is very overkill.

I think a better solution to your problem is to merge the SegmentationRenderer and the SegmentationPyramidRenderer so that it accepts both Image and ImagePyramid data objects.

discussion_timeline.author: smistad
discussion_timeline.body:
[source/FAST/Algorithms/ImagePatch/PatchGenerator.cpp] Think more general. The mask doesn't have to be tissue...
"Mask threshold", "Threshold, in percentage, for how much of the candidate patch must be inside the mask to be accepted"

And "mask-threshold" is probably a better name.

discussion_timeline.author: andreped
discussion_timeline.body:
[source/FAST/Algorithms/ImagePatch/PatchStitcher.cpp] I agree that merging them would be the ideal solution, but that is outside the scope of what I think I would be able to do with the time I have available. Seems like a lot of work and directly affects all those that are regularly using SegmentationRenderer. Perhaps this is something you could do when you get time? 

One of our end-users need to be able to run inference on image plane = 2, for the images he is using, and there it seems that 8192x8192 is too large. I believe the resultant image plane he was using was somewhat in the order of 2k x 4k, just below the 2048 mark for the WSI I was testing on.

discussion_timeline.author: andreped
discussion_timeline.body: [source/FAST/Data/ImagePyramid.cpp] Yes, but for the same reason above, it seemed necessary for the specific use case mentioned. The image plane I was testing on had dimensions in the order of 2k x 4k.

discussion_timeline.author: andreped
discussion_timeline.body: I have adjusted for the comments above.
